article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: Schneider Electric buying PTC for $22.6 billion
post_text:
Schneider Electric, a French company that makes fuses, circuit breakers, and datacenter cooling racks, just agreed to buy Boston-based industrial software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in cash, a 42.3% premium to PTC's last closing price. It is Schneider's largest acquisition ever.

The deal is a useful reminder of where AI money actually lands. Schneider's market cap more than doubled over four years not because it built a large language model, but because every new datacenter needs its power management hardware. Capital poured into the unglamorous infrastructure layer, and now Schneider is using those gains to move up the software stack.

WBR's piece on the value in boring businesses makes exactly this argument. While investors sprint toward pure AI plays at 30x revenue, the cash accumulates in the companies nobody talks about at conferences. The full piece is linked on our profile.
